sentences.text: The thesis's central reason to buy, that Huang's departure is good for the company, is unsupported on this record. The 8-K confirms the resignation, but every financial figure and the valuation price come from before it, so nothing here shows how the business or the price responded.
The claims that do hold, gross margin above 70% and accelerating revenue, describe the business Huang left behind. They argue that the asset is strong, not that his absence improves it.

Of the two challenged claims, the cash claim matters more to a buy decision than the revenue claim: missing a doubling is beside the point when the price needs only 13.4% a year. Earnings running ahead of cash goes to the quality of what the price is paid for.
The price of 28.5× earnings sits against a free cash flow yield of only 2.3%, because each dollar of net income came with 0.70 dollars of operating cash. On cash the stock is dearer than on earnings.
The price's modest growth requirement leans almost entirely on a 65.2% operating margin held every year. Any leadership change that dents margin works against the buy case, not for it.
A careful investor would want two things the record lacks: the first 10-Q covering a quarter after November 11, 2026, and an 8-K naming a permanent chief executive in place of the interim one.
The claim asserts a cause. The filings can confirm that the change happened, but not that it makes the company more valuable, and no figure in the record dates from after it.

The corollaries that came out in its favour, a wider operating margin and a lower opex ratio, measure a quarter run under Huang. The free cash flow margin corollary failed anyway, so even this indirect support is mixed.

The departure sits within a run of senior turnover: the interim chief executive is the existing CFO, the head of worldwide field operations is retiring, and the chief accounting officer retired. The record cannot say whether that much change helps or hurts.
Growth is speeding up, not fading: year-on-year revenue growth rose to 105.9% from 85.2% the quarter before, with Data Center contributing 102.5 percentage points of it.
The margin the price depends on rests on a gross margin that ranks 4 of 63 in its industry. The tightest quarter of the streak still had room of 1.69x a typical move.
The 13.4% a year the 2026-09-30 price needs is far below the company's own +100.0% a year over three fiscal years. Even the top of the assumption grid, 19.7%, sits well below its current pace.

Earnings are outrunning cash and the gap is widening. Over the four quarters free cash flow fell $65.87B short of net income as receivables and inventory absorbed cash, and the company ranks 32 of 38 on cash conversion among its peers.
Inventory has risen to 119.3 days from 105.6. The last excess-inventory episode, the H20 charge, pulled gross margin down to 60.5%, so the build is a direct risk to the margin the price relies on.
At an industry 90th-percentile margin of 26.6% the price would need 28.1% a year, and 0 of 40 ten-year spans of filers this size grew even 13.4%. The valuation also predates the resignation.
A 10-Q for a quarter after the resignation shows quarterly gross margin still above 70%.
That quarter's operating margin stays above 50%.
An 8-K names a permanent chief executive in place of the interim appointment.
Quarterly cash conversion stays at or below 0.40x.
Inventory days rise above 119.3 days.
Accounts receivable climb above $63.06B.
Year-on-year quarterly revenue growth falls below the +85.2% of Q1 FY2027.
Deferred revenue falls below $6.41B.
Quarterly revenue falls below $96.22B.
